;Disasters and accidents
*[[SIEV X]]
**An [[Iraqis|Iraqi]] man is arrested at [[Brisbane Airport]] for his membership in a [[human trafficking]] syndicate responsible for chartering a boat carrying 421 [[Afghans|Afghan]] and Iraqi refugees [[Asylum in Australia|to Australia]]. More than 350 of those aboard perished when the boat sank off the coast of [[Indonesia]] in October 2001. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2019/oct/19/siev-x-tragedy-iraqi-man-charged-in-australia-in-connection-with-deaths-of-350-people (''The Guardian'')]
*A dam on the Seiba river in [[Krasnoyarsk]], [[Siberia]], collapses, flooding a nearby gold mine and cabins used to house miners. At least 15 people have been killed, with 13 more missing and 14 hospitalised. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-50108413 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Santiago protests]]
**The [[Chilean government]] declares a [[state of emergency]] in the capital [[Santiago]], following riots in response to a price hike in [[Santiago Metro]] fares. Overnight, the high-rise headquarters of [[Enel Generación Chile]] is [[arson|set on fire]] by rioters. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-50106743 (BBC News)]
**19 stations of the [[Santiago Metro]] are set on fire during the night. [https://www.latercera.com/nacional/noticia/incendios-estaciones-del-metro/868259/ (''La Tercera'')]
**Police and military officers clash with protestors in [[Plaza Baquedano]], [[Maipú, Chile|Maipú Main Square]] and other places, while several ''[[cacerolazo|cacerolazos]]'' are heard in the city. [https://www.adnradio.cl/noticias/deportes/cacerolazo-convocado-por-vecinos-finalizo-con-incidentes-en-la-plaza-de-maipu/20191019/nota/3968118.aspx (ADN Radio)]
**[[Curfew]] is announced for the [[Greater Santiago]] area, the first time it is used since the end of the [[Augusto Pinochet|Pinochet]] [[Military dictatorship of Chile (1973–1990)|dictatorship]]. [https://www.eldesconcierto.cl/2019/10/19/decretan-inedito-toque-de-queda-en-santiago-tras-fracaso-del-gobierno-en-contener-ola-de-protestas/ (''El Desconcierto'')]
*[[Brexit]]
**The [[Parliament of the United Kingdom|British Parliament]] votes 322 to 306 to pass the so-called "[[Oliver Letwin|Letwin]] amendment" to the [[Brexit withdrawal agreement|Withdrawal Agreement Bill]], which states it will not approve any withdrawal agreement unless all relevant formal legislation is passed. In effect any subsequent vote on a deal is not considered final, and [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] will be forced to ask for an extension. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-britain-eu-letwin-vote/uk-lawmakers-vote-for-letwin-proposals-forcing-johnson-toward-brexit-delay-idUSKBN1WY0D0 (Reuters)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/10/19/uk/brexit-letwin-amendment-scli-intl-gbr/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2019–20 Lebanese protests]]
**Four ministers resign from the [[Lebanese government of January 2019|current cabinet]], stating that the government is incapable of addressing any of the issues under current circumstances. Conversely, [[Hassan Nasrallah]] of [[Hezbollah]] announces that his group will continue to support the government, saying, "All of us have to shoulder the responsibility of the current situation that we arrived at." [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/10/tens-thousands-protest-day-lebanon-191019180840017.html (Al Jazeera)]
